Minimum and maximum positions

Unit 1 · Week 6 · Lesson 3 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Python editor and index/value/best-index trace grids. Establish non-empty input before inspecting index0.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Minimum and maximum positions

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Success means retain the position of a best value, explain first-occurrence ties and state empty-list assumptions. Use non-empty integer lists for the main algorithm, then explicitly discuss the empty case.

2. Retrieval: location and value

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and pair explanation

For values=[4,9,9], maximum value 9 appears at indices 1 and 2. Ask learners for both, then why saying 9 does not locate an occurrence. Retrieve zero-based indexing and length before deciding a tie rule.

3. The first maximum index

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher modelling and guided trace

This example assumes non-empty values. Start best_index 0, comparing actual values via indexing. At index 1,9>4 updates best_index 1; at index 2,9>9 is False so retain 1. Output 1 9. State first-occurrence tie rule. best_index 0 means a valid position, not a guessed maximum value of zero.

4. A trace of the best position

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example with reduced support

Model initial best_index 0/value 4. For index 1 compare 9>4 True and update 1; index 2 compare 9>9 False and retain 1. Learners complete rows independently before pair checking. For a fresh[8,2,7], best_index stays 0. Support: write both compared values. Stretch: explain why a one-element list makes no loop-body passes but still has maximum index 0.

5. Negative values and ties

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided variation and all-student checks

For[-8,-3], first maximum index 1/value-3. A guessed maximum value 0 is wrong because 0 is not present; best_index 0 correctly refers to real value-8. For[4,9,9], > retains first index 1 while >= updates to last index 2. Ask learners to commit predictions then explain the equality check. Support: label index/value separately.

6. Adapting the search for a minimum

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent coding with optional scaffolds

Change > to < and keep non-empty assumption. For[-2,4,-5,-5], first minimum index 2/value-5. For[7], index 0/value 7. Learners code and trace independently then compare evidence in pairs. Strict < preserves first equal minimum, <= gives last. Support: supply header and index loop. Stretch: implement max_index as a Week 5 function returning an index for non-empty input.

7. What about an empty list?

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Hinge question and error analysis

Correct B: no maximum position exists. Accessing values[0] on[] raises IndexError. Check len(values)==0 first, reporting no maximum, and use the algorithm only in the non-empty branch. If several choose A, ask what element index 0 would refer to. A total of 0 for an empty list does not imply maximum index 0.

8. Exit ticket: index, value and tie rule

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit ticket

For[-4,-1,-1], first maximum index 1/value-1; >= would retain 2. First minimum is index 0/value-4. Empty list needs a guard before accessing index 0. Collect individual explanations to identify tie-rule, sign or index confusion before the temperature task.
